subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should OpenClaw add custom Gateway CLI WebSocket headers, and which credential-safe input sources and precedence should become the supported public contract?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but the requested CLI/env/config surfaces can carry reverse-proxy credentials and change the Gateway authentication boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve narrow secret-safe contract
options.body: Add header forwarding only through maintainer-approved sources, with SecretInput/env substitution, redaction, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Limit to explicit CLI headers
options.body: Support only repeatable per-invocation `--header` values for now, avoiding durable config/env persistence at the cost of automation ergonomics.

options.title: Decline core header support
options.body: Keep SSH, Tailscale, and local proxy workflows as the supported paths and document that reverse-proxy header injection stays outside OpenClaw CLI.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow secret-safe contract
recommendation.body: Add header forwarding only through maintainer-approved sources, with SecretInput/env substitution, redaction, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses the Gateway client package, shared call path, and credential-bearing config surface where Peter has the strongest current and historical code signal.
